author: Pastor Marcus Vance
title: Why we go: the heart behind our mission trips
content:
Every year someone asks why a church our size still sends teams across the world when there is so much need across the street. It is a fair question, and the honest answer is that we do not see it as a choice between the two.

The same Jesus who fed the crowd on the hillside also sent his friends out to the ends of the earth. When a team from Grace Community spends ten days building a classroom or running a medical clinic, they come home changed. They notice the neighbor who is struggling. They sign up for Serve Day. They give more freely and pray more specifically.

We also go because we are invited. Every trip we send is in partnership with a local church that asked for help, and our teams work under their leadership. We are not there to fix anyone; we are there to stand alongside brothers and sisters who know their community far better than we ever will.

This year we are sending three teams: a construction team to Guatemala in February, a medical team to Kenya in June, and a youth team to the Dominican Republic in July. Applications are open now, and every team has spots for people who have never been on a trip before. If you cannot go, you can still send: every gift to the missions fund goes straight to travel costs and our partner churches.
bullet_summary: Local service and global missions are not competing priorities; both flow from the same calling.
Every trip partners with a local church that invited us, and our teams serve under their leadership.
Three teams go out this year (Guatemala, Kenya and the Dominican Republic), with room for first-timers.
Those who cannot go can support the trips through the missions fund.
